scores.label: A
scores.note: Option 5 'trickle' means spreading slowly, which contradicts 'quickly'. Option 7 'percolate' also suggests slow filtering, contradicts 'quickly', and is rarer than the essay can carry. Option 9 'pervade' is transitive, so 'pervade across Europe' is ungrammatical. The other options are in base form and need a tense edit to the past tense; 'pass' and 'go' are plain.

scores.label: B
scores.note: Option 1 'widespread' is an adjective and is ungrammatical in place. Option 5 'dissperse' is misspelled. Option 10 'dispersal' is a noun and is ungrammatical in place. Options 2–4 are in base form and need a tense edit. The list is dominated by duplicates.

scores.label: C
scores.note: Option 7 'transmitted' is a transitive verb, so it is awkward or ungrammatical in place without 'were'. The top three are strong past-tense options. Heavy duplication leaves almost no variety.

scores.label: D
scores.note: Option 7 'transmit' is a transitive verb, so it does not work in place without a passive construction. Every option is in base form and needs a tense edit to the past tense. The echo of 'spread' at position 3 takes up a top slot.

scores.label: E
scores.note: Option 10 'broke out' means erupted or began suddenly, which changes the meaning. Option 7 'went' and option 4 'moved' are plain. The past-tense options at the top fit well.
